Q: When should a workflow use optimistic version checks instead of a row lock?
A: Optimistic concurrency includes the version observed by a reader in the update condition and detects a conflicting change through the affected-row result. A row lock serializes access to selected rows while held, but can increase waiting and deadlock risk. Both require an explicit transaction boundary and do not automatically protect a multi-row invariant. Choose based on contention, interaction duration and retry cost. Never hold a database lock while a person reviews a form or a slow external provider responds.
Why: Two editors read version 5. The first updates it to 6; the second update conditioned on version 5 affects zero rows and should surface a conflict rather than overwrite the accepted change.
Risk: Blind retries can discard user intent or repeat external effects.
Trade: Optimistic checks fit low contention; locks can simplify short contested transitions.
